text: Syed Bashir Ahmad (Kashmiri: سید بشیر احمد) (born 2 January 1952 in Sheikhar, Pulwama district in Jammu and Kashmir)[1][2] is a Kashmiri politician who has worked for the social upliftment of people in rural areas and has advocated for the rights of weaker sections. He served as the Member of Legislative Assembly from Rajpora Constituency[3] and was the Chairman of the Petitions Committee of the Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly.[4] He entered politics at a young age and was associated with the Janata Dal, Indian National Congress, and Jan Morcha. In the 1996 state assembly elections, he contested from the Pulwama constituency on a Janata Dal ticket against the National Conference candidate but lost by a narrow margin.[5] In 1999, he co-founded the Jammu & Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party (PDP), which was led by Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, the former Home Minister of India and Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister. In 2002, he won the Assembly Elections from Rajpora Constituency and was appointed Minister for Education in Mufti Mohammad Sayeed's government.[2][6] He later held the portfolios of 'PHE, Irrigation and Flood Control' and 'Roads & Buildings'.[7] He won again from Rajpora in the 2008 Assembly Elections.[6] In July 2005, militants attempted to assassinate him at crowded Budshah Chowk in Srinagar while he was en route from the Civil Secretariat; he escaped unharmed, but two of his personnel security officers (PSO) and a civilian were injured.[8][9] In July 2014, the PDP removed Syed Bashir Ahmad from its candidate list for the 2014 Assembly elections. Shortly thereafter, hundreds of his party workers from Rajpora Constituency staged a large protest outside Housing Colony in Pulwama, where top politicians and legislative members reside, criticizing Mufti Mohammad Sayeed for ignoring Syed Bashir. The protesters later drove to Srinagar and held a demonstration outside the PDP president’s official Gupkar residence, demanding a mandate in favor of Syed Bashir. Syed Bashir later stated that he was not consulted before being dropped from the list and was only informed over the phone that he was no longer the candidate.[11] In October 2014, Syed Bashir was expelled from the PDP, according to a party statement citing anti-party activities.[12] In a press interview, he denied the allegations, saying he was not given any notice of the expulsion, had not engaged in any anti-party activities, and had respected the party symbol even when denied the mandate.[13] On 30 October 2014, Syed Bashir announced his intention to contest the J&K Legislative Assembly elections 2014 as an independent candidate. At a press conference held at his Sheikhar residence, he stated that although several political parties offered him a ticket, he declined them as his workers and supporters wanted him to run independently, and he had no choice but to honor their wishes.[14][15] On 22 August 2024, Syed Bashir Ahmad rejoined the People's Democratic Party.[16]
